atoms.b: Most Anglo-Saxon children didn’t go to school and were expected to start ((++working singing)) at the age of 10.
Children would ((++learn forget)) their trade from their parents.
For example, the son of a blacksmith would learn about ((++smithing woodcutting)), while a girl would learn how to manage the ((++household army)) from her mother.

atoms.b: The only schools in Anglo-Saxon Britain were run by the ((++Church King)) and were for training ((++monks warriors)), nuns and priests.
Most rich children were taught at home by a private ((++tutor baker)), but some were sent to live with the Church instead. These ((++children animals)) were known as oblates.

feedback.finish: Most oblates were from families that did not have enough land to split between all of their children. The Church was a way for the younger children to still have influence and safety.

atoms.text: In Anglo-Saxon Britain, childhood deaths were common, as even small injuries could be life-threatening without modern medicine.
In times of famine and conflict, children would often die of starvation or illness. It is estimated that one third of all Anglo-Saxons did not live past their fifth birthday.
